program_overview.title: Creative Coding and Animation Mastery
program_overview.tagline: Where art meets code: real video editing, motion graphics, generative art with p5.js and Blender 3D, finished as a portfolio that moves.
program_overview.description:
This course sits at the intersection most creative courses miss: editing and motion design craft on one side, actual creative coding on the other. Students learn professional video editing, motion graphics, animation principles, then cross into p5.js and Processing, where art is written in code and no two runs look the same, and finish with Blender 3D and the content craft that makes work travel online.

The toolkit is free-first and honest: DaVinci Resolve, CapCut, Blender, p5.js and Canva cover the entire syllabus at zero software cost, with Adobe After Effects taught as the industry-standard option for students who have access to it. Every week produces finished work, and the course ends with a portfolio capstone and a final exam that decides the certificate.

The pace is honest: five months at two live classes a week plus three to four hours of practice, with a sixth month in hand for students who need more time. Homework after every class, a mixed challenge at the end of each month, and a final exam with a free retest after revision. Real craft, real portfolio, depth over dopamine.
what_makes_this_different: Creative coding is real here: p5.js and Processing get a full month, generative art most animation courses never touch
Free-first toolkit: DaVinci Resolve, CapCut, Blender, p5.js and Canva cover the whole syllabus; After Effects taught as the industry option, never a paywall
Craft over hacks: animation principles, typography and rhythm, the fundamentals that survive every platform trend
Every week ends rendered: finished edits, loops, sketches and scenes, building one coherent portfolio
An honest 5-month arc with a sixth month in hand: nobody is rushed
Real assessment: weekly homework, monthly mixed challenges, and a final exam that decides the certificate, with a free retest after revision

learning_path.month_1: Foundations and editing (Weeks 1-4): design principles, animation basics, desktop and mobile video editing
learning_path.month_2: Motion graphics (Weeks 5-8): keyframes, easing, kinetic typography and compositing, in After Effects or free equivalents
learning_path.month_3: Creative coding (Weeks 9-12): Processing and p5.js, generative art, interactivity and code-driven animation
learning_path.month_4: 3D and short-form craft (Weeks 13-16): Blender fundamentals, 3D scenes and renders, and the short-form video craft that travels
learning_path.month_5: Channel, portfolio and the exam (Weeks 17-20): long-form storytelling, honest analytics, a portfolio that opens doors, and the final capstone

career_outcomes: A rendered portfolio: edits, motion pieces, generative art and 3D scenes, presented properly
Skills that stack into creative work: editing, motion design, creative coding and 3D fundamentals
The judgment layer: taste, references and critique habits that separate makers from tool users
Honest next steps: deeper motion design, our web development track for creative developers, or freelance-style small projects

month_1.title: Month 1: Creative Foundations & Video Editing Basics
month_1.description: Master design principles, animation fundamentals, and professional video editing.

week_1.title: Design Principles & Digital Art Basics
topics: Elements of design: line, shape, color, texture, space
Principles of design: balance, contrast, emphasis, movement
Color theory: RGB/CMYK, color harmony, psychology
File formats: when to use what
projects: Personal Brand Identity: Logo, color palette, style guide
Mood Board Collection: 5 different aesthetic mood boards
Social Media Template Set: Consistent design templates
week_1.practice: Pick a real poster or flyer you like, rebuild it with a stronger visual hierarchy and a deliberate color harmony, and note which design principle drove each change.

week_2.title: Animation Principles & 2D Basics
projects: Bouncing Ball Animation: Master timing and physics
Character Walk Cycle: Create smooth character movement
Animated Logo Reveal: Bring brand to life
week_2.practice: Animate a simple bouncing ball that shows squash and stretch plus ease in and ease out, and export a five second clip.

week_3.title: Video Editing Fundamentals
projects: Day in Life Vlog: Edit personal vlog footage
Music Video Edit: Sync video to music
week_3.practice: Cut a 60 second highlight video from any raw footage using at least three transition types and synced background audio.

week_4.title: Mobile Video Editing & Quick Content
projects: YouTube Shorts Collection: Engaging short-form content
week_4.practice: Shoot and edit a 30 second vertical reel on your phone with captions, one filter and a mobile color grade.
week_4.assessment: Month 1 check: a timed edit from provided footage, plus a mixed quiz on design and animation principles

month_2.title: Month 2: Motion Graphics & After Effects Mastery
month_2.description: Master motion design, visual effects, and professional animation techniques.

week_5.title: After Effects Fundamentals
projects: Animated Title Sequence: Professional title animation
week_5.practice: Recreate a short channel intro in After Effects by keyframing position, scale and rotation on three layers, then smooth the motion in the graph editor.

week_6.title: Advanced Motion Graphics
projects: Social Media Pack: Animated social elements
week_6.practice: Build a ten second logo reveal using trim paths and one morphing shape transition.

week_7.title: Character Animation & Rigging
week_7.practice: Rig a simple two legged character with Duik and animate a basic four step walk cycle.

week_8.title: Visual Effects & Compositing
projects: Product VFX Commercial: Product with effects
Music Video Effects: Visual effects for music
week_8.practice: Key out a green screen clip, place the subject on a new background and match the color and shadows so the composite holds up.
week_8.assessment: Month 2 check: a 10-second motion piece built live, with questions reaching back to month 1

month_3.title: Month 3: Creative Coding & Interactive Media
month_3.description: Master creative programming with Processing, p5.js, and interactive installations.

week_9.title: Processing Fundamentals
projects: Generative Art System: Algorithmic art creation
week_9.practice: Code a Processing sketch that draws a repeating pattern using loops, variables and at least three colors.

week_10.title: p5.js and Web-Based Creative Coding
topics: p5.js setup and differences from Processing
projects: Interactive Website: Creative coding in web design
Audio Visualizer Web App: Music-reactive visuals
week_10.practice: Port one of your Processing sketches to p5.js and add mouse interaction plus one sound trigger.

week_11.title: Interactive Installations & Physical Computing
week_11.practice: Plan a small sensor driven installation on paper and prototype its visual response in Processing using simulated input values.

week_12.title: Creative Coding Applications
projects: Live Performance Tool: VJ/DJ visual system
week_12.practice: Generate three variations of one generative art piece by changing the rules and the randomness, then pick the strongest for your portfolio.
week_12.assessment: Month 3 check: a small generative sketch written live, plus mixed review of earlier months

month_4.title: Month 4: Blender 3D and Short-Form Craft
month_4.description: Three weeks of honest Blender fundamentals, then the short-form editing craft that makes work travel.

week_13.title: 3D Animation Fundamentals with Blender
week_13.practice: Model a simple low poly object in Blender using primitives and modifiers, then apply basic materials and render one image.

week_14.title: Character Animation & Rigging in 3D
topics: Physics simulation for cloth and hair
week_14.practice: Add an armature to a basic character mesh, weight paint two joints and pose the character in three distinct positions.

week_15.title: Advanced VFX & Compositing
projects: VFX Breakdown Reel: Professional VFX shots
week_15.practice: Track a short live action clip and composite one graphic or CG element so it sticks to the scene convincingly.

week_16.title: Short-Form Video Craft
topics: The grammar of reels and shorts: hooks, pacing, payoff
Editing rhythm: cuts on beats, breath and surprise
Captions and text animation that people actually read
Covers, thumbnails and the three-second test
Repurposing one piece across formats honestly
Trends as ingredients, craft as the recipe
A week of daily publishing practice, reviewed
projects: Three finished short-form pieces from one shoot or one render
A motion-graphics short built for vertical
week_16.practice: Edit one short piece daily; review the best two in class
week_16.assessment: Month 4 check: a timed edit challenge plus a mixed quiz over months 1-4

month_5.title: Month 5: Channel, Portfolio and the Finale
month_5.description: Long-form storytelling, honest analytics, a portfolio that opens doors, and the final capstone exam.

week_17.title: Long-Form Video and Storytelling
topics: Story structure for longer pieces: promise, journey, payoff
projects: YouTube Channel Launch: Complete channel setup
week_17.practice: Design two alternative thumbnails and titles for the same video idea and explain which pairing you would A/B test first.

week_18.title: Publishing Strategy and Honest Analytics
topics: Reading analytics without fooling yourself: retention over vanity numbers
projects: Content Repurposing System: Efficient content creation
week_18.practice: Repurpose one long form video into a short, a carousel and a text post, each genuinely adapted to its platform.

week_19.title: Portfolio Development & Personal Branding
projects: Brand Identity Package: Complete personal brand
week_19.practice: Draft your portfolio homepage with three case studies, each telling the problem, process and result in one paragraph.

week_20.title: Capstone, Demo Day and Final Exam
topics: The capstone: one polished portfolio piece that uses editing, motion and code or 3D
A working-brief simulation: brief, drafts, revisions, delivery, the professional loop
Final portfolio assembly and presentation order
Presenting creative work: intent, references, decisions
Full-course mixed review before the exam
projects: The capstone piece, rendered and presented at demo day with the full portfolio
week_20.practice: Daily capstone progress with an edit log
week_20.assessment: FINAL EXAM: capstone presentation plus a practical challenge and written questions mixed from the whole course. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest

faqs.question: What skills does this creative coding and animation course cover?
faqs.answer: The 6-month program moves through video editing, motion graphics in After Effects, creative coding with Processing and p5.js, 3D animation in Blender, and content strategy for Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. Students finish with a capstone project and a professional portfolio of animations, edits, and interactive art.

faqs.question: Who is this course suitable for?
faqs.answer: It is designed for ages 14 and up, so it works for teens as well as adults exploring a creative career or a serious side skill. We teach students from ages 6 to 65 across coding and maths, and this course sits at the older, creator-focused end of that range.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn video editing and animation?
faqs.answer: To a genuine portfolio level across editing, motion graphics, creative coding and 3D basics: 5 months at 2 live classes a week plus 3 to 4 hours of practice. The course keeps a sixth month in hand for students who need more time, with no rushing and no penalty. First finished edits appear in week 3; the compounding starts immediately.

faqs.question: How is progress assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Every class ends with a piece to finish, every month ends with a mixed challenge that revisits earlier skills, and the course ends with a final exam: a capstone presentation plus practical and written challenges drawn from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Do students need design or coding experience first?
faqs.answer: No. The course starts with design and animation principles from zero, and the creative coding modules introduce programming gently through visual output, so beginners see results from the first weeks.

faqs.question: Which software is used, and do we have to buy anything?
faqs.answer: No purchases are required: DaVinci Resolve (free version), CapCut, Blender, Processing, p5.js and free Canva cover the entire syllabus. After Effects, the motion-graphics industry standard, is taught as an option for students who already have Adobe access, and every concept it demonstrates is also shown in the free tools. A mid-range computer handles the whole course.

faqs.question: Where can these skills lead after the course?
faqs.answer: Graduates leave with a portfolio spanning editing, motion graphics, and creative code, a strong foundation for freelance work, a content channel, or deeper study in design and development. Many students pair this course with our web development track to add interactive websites to their creative range.

faqs.question: What are the monthly fees?
faqs.answer: In India: ₹1,499 per month for group classes (2 classes weekly, maximum 10 students), ₹2,999 per month for a mini batch of 3-4 learners, and ₹4,999 per month for personal 1-on-1 training with 2 private classes a week. International students pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency classes.

faqs.question: Is there a demo class before committing?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is completely free with no obligation to continue. Reserve a slot at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact; for teen learners, parents are welcome to sit in on the session.

faqs.question: What is the class format?
faqs.answer: Live 1-hour online classes with a real instructor, never recorded lectures. Sessions are interactive and kept to small groups, so every student presents work, receives direct feedback, and asks questions freely.

faqs.question: Do students receive certification?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is earned: the certificate is awarded on passing the final exam, a capstone presentation plus practical and written challenges, with a free retest after revision if needed. The portfolio matters more though: finished edits, motion pieces, generative art and 3D renders that show exactly what you can make.
